outcome: Maternal recovery outcomes (complete recovery, partial recovery without dialysis, progression to chronic kidney disease, death)
cohort: The study included 46 pregnant women above 18 years of age admitted with pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (PRAKI) and post-delivery, excluding those with pre-existing renal disease or AKI unrelated to pregnancy.
finding: The primary causes of PRAKI were obstetric complications (32.6% due to postpartum hemorrhage) and pregnancy-specific disorders (26.1% due to pre-eclampsia), with most patients achieving complete (47.8%) or partial (41.3%) recovery, though 10.9% progressed to chronic kidney disease and 13.0% died.
